title: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
abstract: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.
summary: This paper establishes a deep connection between graph theory and quantum integrable models by showing that the quantized six-vertex (Q6V) model can realize Hamiltonians whose spectra are free-parafermionic. It achieves this by demonstrating that the Q6V transfer matrix naturally encodes the structure of any arbitrary indifference graph. This provides a powerful, concrete realization of a key criterion in the study of exactly solvable quantum systems.
main_problem: To provide a concrete realization of a graph-theoretic criterion stating that a Hamiltonian exhibits a free-parafermion spectrum if its frustration graph is an indifference graph.
main_result: The paper shows that any finite indifference graph can be realized as the frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex (Q6V) model at odd roots of unity.
method: The authors map the graph-theoretic structure (indifference graphs) onto the algebraic structure of the Q6V model's transfer matrix, demonstrating an equivalence between the independent-set operator and the transfer matrix.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Quantized Six-Vertex (Q6V) model, analyzed at odd roots of unity. The physics is governed by a Hamiltonian whose spectrum is related to independent sets of a graph, which is formalized via the Q6V layer transfer matrix.
key_observables: Free-parafermion spectrum, the independent-set operator $T_G(y)$, and the layer transfer matrix $T_G(y)$ of the Q6V model.
important_parameters: Odd roots of unity ($\epsilon$), the graph structure (indifference graphs), and parameters defining the Q6V wiring diagram ($p, L$).
main_assumptions: The equivalence between the indifference ordering and the umbrella property is assumed from prior work, and the Q6V approach is restricted to odd roots of unity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the flow from an arbitrary indifference graph to the Q6V realization, show examples of indifference orderings and path powers, and detail the admissible wiring diagram for the Q6V model.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the graph-theoretic criterion, then details the Q6V model setup, and finally proves the equivalence by showing that the Q6V transfer matrix naturally generates the independent-set operator for any indifference graph.
why_interesting: This work connects abstract graph theory (indifference graphs) directly to a concrete, integrable quantum statistical model (Q6V), providing a powerful tool for understanding exactly solvable quantum many-body systems.
